slides.say: A modal inside a box with overflow hidden gets clipped. A portal renders it somewhere else in the DOM.
Call create portal with some JSX and a DOM node, like document dot body. The modal’s DOM lands there, outside the clipping box.

slides.text: Only the DOM placement changes. In React, it’s still a child: it reads parent context.
slides.say: A portal only changes where the DOM node goes. In every other way, it is still a child of the component that renders it, and can read its context.

slides.text: The target DOM node must already exist.
slides.say: The target DOM node must already exist when you create the portal.
